html:
In 1709 Mirwais Hotak, a Ghilji Pashtun chief, killed the Safavid governor of Kandahar, in southern Afghanistan, and made the city independent, founding the Hotak dynasty.

Kandahar had long been fought over by the Safavids of Iran and the Mughals. Mirwais beat back Persian armies sent to retake it. His son Mahmud went further: in 1722 he marched into Iran, besieged Isfahan for months and forced the Safavid shah to give up his throne. The Hotaks ruled Isfahan for a few years of terror before being driven out.

Nader Shah ended the dynasty when he took Kandahar in 1738. But the Hotaks had shown that Pashtun tribes could build a state, and nine years later Ahmad Shah Durrani, one of Nader's officers, founded the Durrani Empire, seen as the start of modern Afghanistan.
sum: In 1709 Mirwais Hotak, a Ghilji Pashtun chief, killed the Safavid governor of Kandahar, in southern Afghanistan, and made the city independent, founding the Hotak dynasty.
